results.summary: Brent confirms essential-cost and emergency support for eligible residents aged 18 and over, online applications, Hub help and its contact number. The rolling limit covers both partners in a couple. An award is not guaranteed.

sources.note: The scheme page gives the savings and residence rules, evidence requirements, application route and the restriction on repeat applications by partners.

findings.currentValue: Evidence required. Normally one application per rolling 12 months, even if a previous application was declined. Awards are discretionary.
findings.proposedValue: Evidence required. One application per rolling 12 months, even if declined. For couples, an application by either partner counts towards this limit; it does not apply to other adult household members. Awards are discretionary.
findings.reason: The council states a firm rolling limit and partner restriction omitted from the current text.
findings.evidence: Council says an application from either partner counts for the 12-month period, while other adults in the household are not subject to this partner rule.

results.summary: Camden’s indexed council contact page describes asking about care needs and the specific reasons for using the phone instead of the form. The full page returned a 520 response today; fees, individual eligibility and response times were not established.

sources.note: Council text in search results describes online and telephone routes; the full page could not be retrieved today.

findings.currentValue: Use the online contact form or call and say “Adult Social Care”.
findings.proposedValue: Complete the online form for yourself or someone else. If you have difficulty with the form, need urgent support or are concerned about immediate safety, call and say “Adult Social Care”.
findings.reason: The council specifies when to use the telephone route rather than listing it as a general alternative.
findings.evidence: The council directs requests to the online form and gives the contact number for form difficulties, urgent needs or immediate safety concerns.

results.summary: Camden lists services, organisations and local groups in a directory searchable by keyword or topic. Its directory homepage does not establish individual providers’ eligibility, fees, contact details or opening times.

sources.note: The council homepage shows the service search box and categories including community groups, health, housing, leisure and sport.

results.summary: Citizens Advice Camden confirms free independent and confidential advice for residents, a weekday freephone line from 10am to 4pm and an online callback request. Callback timing depends on demand; no appointment availability was established.

sources.note: Homepage confirms the local advice offer, resident criterion, telephone contact and weekday hours.
The callback page describes applying online and says response depends on demand.

results.summary: Hestia confirms free listening and practical support for adults who live in Camden or have used its mental health services. It accepts walk-ins and calls during evening opening times, including bank holidays, at the listed location. Current availability was not confirmed.

sources.note: The sanctuary page gives its age and borough criteria, self-contact routes, hours, site address and service contact.

results.summary: Camden Disability Action describes disabled-led advice, advocacy and local opportunities to shape services. Its help page confirms telephone and text contact, a BSL interpreting link and 10am to 4pm advice hours. It does not specify days or fees.

sources.note: The help page gives advice line hours, phone and text contacts, and a route to a BSL video interpreter.
The organisation describes its disabled-led structure, advice, advocacy and activities for disabled people in Camden.

results.summary: Change Grow Live confirms free drug and alcohol support for people over 18 in Camden, family support, telephone enquiries and appointments at several sites. It distinguishes the self-referral form from the professional route, which requires the person’s permission. Waiting times were not established.

sources.note: Service overview gives the local offer, age wording, free access, contact and locations, and separates the two online routes.
People can ask for help with their own substance use using the self-referral form.
The third-party form asks for professional details and for confirmation that the person has given permission.

findings.currentValue: Refer yourself or someone else online, or call to discuss support.
findings.proposedValue: You can refer yourself online or call to ask about support. Professionals referring someone else need that person’s permission.
findings.reason: The listing presents referring someone else as a general route. The provider identifies a separate professional form and explicitly requires consent.
findings.evidence: The service links separately to self-referral and professional referrals. The latter requires the referring professional to confirm the person has agreed to be contacted.

results.summary: Camden’s benefits hub links to money advice, Council Tax Support, benefits claims, and grants, funds and loans. The overview does not establish individual entitlement, award levels, a general telephone route or the evidence each scheme requires.

sources.note: The benefits and financial support homepage groups help by topic and links to instructions for individual schemes.

results.summary: The centre confirms support with abuse, welfare and benefits, employment and mental wellbeing. Its published centre contact matches the listing and is distinct from its homecare contact. Hopscotch describes its advocacy as London-wide; the Camden listing does not claim exclusive eligibility. Programme-specific entry conditions, appointment availability, costs and languages for an individual session were not established.

sources.note: The homepage identifies the charity and lists the address and telephone contact for the women’s centre separately from the homecare service.
The programme overview describes culturally sensitive services for women and girls, including domestic abuse, employment, welfare advice and wellbeing, with links to individual programmes.

results.summary: Camden describes help both for someone who has nowhere to live and for someone unable to manage at home. A person can tell the discharge team or use the housing form themselves. A council assessment and local connection matter; an offer of accommodation is not assured. We did not confirm individual eligibility, vacancies, costs or a direct telephone number.

sources.note: Camden distinguishes help with daily living from homelessness advice, names both the ward route and the direct form, and explains the local-connection and assessment process.

results.summary: The Job Hub offers free employment support to Camden residents, with workshops, job and training opportunities and a choice of in-person, telephone or video appointments. The Disability Job Hub has a specific registration instruction. Waiting times and a general public telephone number were not established.

sources.note: Council page describes free support, inclusive resident eligibility, appointment formats, registration and the separate instruction for accessing the Disability Job Hub.

findings.currentValue: Register through Good Work Camden and explain the support or adjustments you would like.
findings.proposedValue: Register with Good Work Camden or use the Job Hub email link to contact an adviser. For the Disability Job Hub, the council asks you to say you are disabled when you register.
findings.reason: The current instruction omits the disability declaration specifically requested for the specialist hub and the general email enquiry route.
findings.evidence: The council offers registration or email for general advice. For the Disability Job Hub, it asks residents to register and identify themselves as disabled on that registration.

results.summary: Hestia confirms the Camden catchment, adult age threshold, walk-in or telephone access, address, opening hours and daily activities. Groups follow an initial session. The separate online referral route is for organisations; an individual does not need it to visit. The page did not establish fees or the availability of a place at a particular time.

sources.note: The provider programme page identifies the five eligible boroughs and minimum age, gives separate public access and organisational referral instructions, and lists its address, times, contact and daily groups.

results.summary: The council identifies the service, links to its contact and access pages and publishes the same team phone number. The service page links to Easy Read information. Full eligibility, the scope of individual support, fees and availability were not confirmed. The form could not be assessed from this reading; no form was tested or submitted.

sources.note: The council overview names the service, links to its help and contact pages, and signposts Easy Read materials.
The team's public contact page lists the same number as the Navigator record and describes its weekday office hours.
The linked form displayed an upload-field permission message. Its completion requirements and usability could not be checked.

results.summary: Camden Council lists local branches, events, digital books and its Home Library Service. Anyone can join; the membership page explains what to bring to borrow items. The home service is free for people unable to visit because they are housebound, older or have mobility difficulties. Individual activity costs, bookings and availability were not checked.

sources.note: Lists branch opening times, membership, activities, digital reading and Home Library Service links.
Confirms anyone can join online; explains ordinary book borrowing, free membership and documents needed to use the library.
Describes free home visits and direct enquiries for people unable to get to the library.

results.summary: The council confirms the advice topics, including Irish documents. The centre publishes its own direct contact route and says advice requires an appointment. No blanket eligibility or fee rule for all enquiries, available appointments or immediate response was established.

sources.note: Camden lists the provider and its benefits, housing and Irish document advice.
The advice page sets out booking instructions, the telephone menu, reception access and the limits of support.

findings.currentValue: Find the London Irish Centre contact route in Camden Advice Network.
findings.proposedValue: Ask the centre for an appointment by phone (choose option 1 twice) or use the email link on its advice page. If neither works for you, check its Camden Square reception hours.
findings.reason: The existing listing directs callers through a council directory instead of giving the direct booking route.
findings.evidence: The provider accepts booking enquiries by telephone or email. Its Camden Square reception is an alternative for people unable to use these routes.

findings.currentValue: Ask about appointments and which advice the centre can currently offer.
findings.proposedValue: Advice is by appointment. Check reception hours before visiting. The centre gives housing advice but does not find private accommodation.
findings.reason: The current wording asks visitors to check whether an appointment is needed; the provider says it is required.
findings.evidence: The service page requires booked appointments and distinguishes housing advice from finding private accommodation.

findings.reason: Link directly to the advice service and its booking information.
findings.evidence: The current council list links onward to the provider; the provider’s own advice page contains contact routes and service limitations.

findings.reason: Add the public booking number for people who cannot use online contact.
findings.evidence: The advice service publishes this number and asks callers to choose option 1 twice.

results.summary: The centre confirms free specialist advice with eligibility varying by service. Housing enquiries are limited to Mondays online; the centre reports reduced capacity and a separate pro bono booking pause. Individual eligibility, appointment availability and a reopening date were not confirmed.

sources.note: The current homepage separates housing, debt, benefits and pro bono intake, including a pro bono pause.
The housing page confirms Monday intake, limited phone assistance, the five-day response rule and the Camden exception to Legal Help eligibility.
The clinic describes limited-capacity, one-off telephone advice by appointment; the homepage carries the current booking notice.

findings.currentValue: Call or use the relevant enquiry form to ask whether the centre can help.
findings.proposedValue: For housing, use the online form on Monday. If you cannot complete it, call Monday or Wednesday, 10am–noon; help filling it in is available on Monday only. For debt or benefits, use the separate contact instructions on the homepage.
findings.reason: The general access wording omits the one-day housing form and the phone alternative.
findings.evidence: Housing intake is online on Mondays. The provider gives two morning phone windows for people unable to use the form, but assisted form completion is only offered on Monday.

findings.currentValue: Ask about eligibility and capacity before travelling. The centre may not be able to take every case.
findings.proposedValue: Housing capacity is limited. If you get no reply within five days, seek another adviser. As of 21 November 2026, no pro bono appointments are available; check the homepage before trying to book.
findings.reason: The centre gives a specific reduced-capacity notice for housing and reports that pro bono appointments are unavailable.
findings.evidence: The homepage says to seek another housing adviser after five days without a response. Its hoped-for reopening of the pro bono form is not a confirmed appointment date.

findings.currentValue: People on a low income in London; case and funding criteria apply.
findings.proposedValue: Londoners on low incomes are the priority. For housing advice, people who live, work or study in Camden do not need to qualify for Legal Help. Eligibility differs by service.
findings.reason: The listing does not explain the local exception for housing enquiries.
findings.evidence: The housing team expressly exempts people who live, work or study in Camden from the Legal Help eligibility requirement for advice, while prioritising low income.

results.summary: The provider describes free Phoenix groups, no drop-ins and a separate paid counselling service. Group places and waiting times were not established.

sources.note: Phoenix groups, direct enquiries, office phone and no drop-in service.
Weekly in-person individual therapy after assessment, £35 per session.

findings.currentValue: Check joining arrangements. Mind in Camden says it does not offer a counselling or drop-in service.
findings.proposedValue: There is no drop-in service. Phoenix support groups are free. Separate one-to-one counselling costs £35 per weekly session after an assessment.
findings.reason: The listing rules out a counselling service that is now advertised.
findings.evidence: The dedicated counselling page describes individual sessions, assessment and the fee; the main page distinguishes free groups from drop-ins.

results.summary: Nafsiyat describes free short-term individual therapy for Camden residents and lists a self-referral route. A place, current intake and waiting times are not confirmed.

sources.note: Intercultural therapy and language support.
Names the four boroughs, free short-term service, self-referral and professional route.
Referral page lists the centre’s public contact details; no open appointment was confirmed.

findings.currentValue: Ask whether funded or paid therapy applies, and about assessment and waiting times.
findings.proposedValue: The short-term individual therapy programme is free for Camden residents. Ask about current availability; the centre also has a separate paid service.
findings.reason: The listing does not distinguish the free local programme from other services.
findings.evidence: The individual therapy page explicitly includes Camden, describes the sessions as free and signposts the separate paid service.

findings.currentValue: Contact the centre to ask about referral and the languages and support available.
findings.proposedValue: Use the self-referral link on the individual therapy page, or contact the centre to ask about languages and availability. Health professionals have a referral route too.
findings.reason: The programme explicitly lists self-referral as well as professional referral.
findings.evidence: The programme page offers both routes and warns that therapists may be fully booked.

results.summary: The council and provider describe support for young people aged 16–24 facing homelessness in London. The centre explains how to seek help directly. Accommodation and places are not guaranteed.

sources.note: Council network identifies the youth service and remit.
Youth homelessness charity links directly to Get Help.
Service describes morning drop-in, age range, housing help and self-referral.

findings.reason: The listing sends people to a council directory instead of the provider’s access information.
findings.evidence: The Get Help page gives direct routes for young people.

findings.currentValue: Use Camden Advice Network’s New Horizon listing to reach the centre and ask for help.
findings.proposedValue: If you are aged 16 to 24 and facing homelessness in London, you can come to the day centre in the morning or use the self-referral route on its Get Help page.
findings.reason: People can approach the provider directly.
findings.evidence: The provider describes its morning drop-in and invites young people at risk of homelessness to attend or self-refer.

results.summary: The organisation describes its self-advocacy work and publishes referral forms. Session availability and charges were not established.

sources.note: Self-advocacy organisation and public service links.
Referral and activity forms and contact route.

results.summary: The provider describes local activities and adult learning at the SHELL Centre, including drop-in learning and some free courses. Individual course dates, costs and places were not checked.

sources.note: Local community, activities and published contact number.
Adult learning through informal drop-ins and structured courses.

results.summary: The NHS confirms online self-referral, phone alternatives, GP referral and assessment. The referral page does not establish individual eligibility or current appointment availability.

sources.note: Published self-referral and telephone routes, and assessment process.

results.summary: The trust confirms the urgent mental health route and distinguishes it from immediate danger. Local response times and capacity were not established.

sources.note: Trust guidance describes urgent support, emergency assessment and what to do when safety is at risk.

results.summary: The centre describes advice, wellbeing activities, classes, local coverage and its timetable. Session-specific charges, booking and access arrangements were not established.

sources.note: Public information on who the centre supports, its activities and programme links.
